Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:10:1.hebrew: אלא רבי אומר סירוס - אע"פ שהן טמונין בכיס לעולם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:10:1.english: Rather, Rabbi says: Castration - Even though they [the testicles] are always concealed in the scrotum.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:10:2.english: And it is not necessary [to mention the] tongue - For it is exposed periodically.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:10:3.english: And what is [the meaning of] "also" - That Ben Azzai said.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:10:4.hebrew: אקמייתא - קאי אעשרים וארבעה המנויין אצל נגעים, דקאמר ת"ק "עבד יוצא בהן לחירות" — מוסיף בן עזאי לענין עבד: אף הלשון:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:10:4.english: To the first [statement] - [It] refers to the twenty-four [limbs] enumerated in connection with *nega'im* [leprous marks], regarding which the first *tanna* said, "A slave goes free on account of them" — Ben Azzai adds regarding a slave: "Also the tongue."

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:11:1.hebrew: אלא לא גרסינן והכי גרסינן תנא שמעה לדרבי וקבעה כו' - קבעה אצל הראשונות, והדר שמעה לדבן עזאי, שהיה מוסיף לשון לבדו על הראשונות ונמצא חלוק על רבי בסירוס, וקבעה בלשון ״אף״ כמו שאמרה בן עזאי. והיה לו לתנא לקובעה בין ת"ק לרבי, והדר למיתני תוספת סירוס עלה; אלא שמאחר שנקבעה של רבי אצל ת"ק והיתה שגורה בפי התלמידים כך — לא זזה של רבי ממקומו, וסידרו של בן עזאי אחריה, לפי שהגירסא השגורה בפה קשה לשנותה ולחזור ולגורסה בלשון אחר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:11:1.english: We do not read "Rather," and this is how we read: "The tanna heard [the statement] of Rabbi and established it, etc." - He established it next to the first [rulings], and then he heard [the statement] of ben Azzai, who added only [the] tongue to the first [rulings] and was found to disagree with Rabbi regarding castration, and he established it with the wording "also," just as ben Azzai had said it. And the tanna should have established it between the first tanna and Rabbi, and then taught the addition of castration after it; however, since Rabbi's [statement] had already been established next to the first tanna and was fluent in the mouths of the students in that manner, Rabbi's [statement] did not move from its place, and he arranged [the statement] of ben Azzai after it, because a version that is fluent in the mouth is difficult to alter and go back and recite in a different wording.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:12:1.hebrew: לענין טומאה - דקי"ל: מגע בית הסתרים אינו מטמא, ונפקא לן במסכת נדה (דף מג.) מ"וכל אשר יגע בו הזב וגו'". הא שטף — טהור?! בתמיה: הא טבילה בעי! אלא, כל אשר יגע בו הזב בדבר שהוא גלוי כידיו, והזב לא שטף עדיין כל גופו במים — שלא טבל מזובו — וכבס בגדיו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:12:1.english: With regard to ritual impurity - For we maintain that contact involving a concealed part [of the body] does not transmit ritual impurity, and we derive this in Tractate Niddah (43a) from: “And whomever the zav touches...” [Does this imply that] if he rinsed [his hands], he is pure?! [This is asked] in astonishment: But he requires immersion [of his whole body]! Rather, [it means:] Whomever the zav touches with [a body part] that is exposed like his hands, and the zav has not yet rinsed his entire body in water — [meaning] that he has not immersed from his zivah — [that person] shall wash his clothes.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:12:2.english: “Whom he touches,” the Merciful One states - This is the verse of “and his hands he did not rinse in water” [Leviticus 15:11].

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:12:3.hebrew: בר נגיעה - כידיו הוא בגלוי, שהרי מוציא לשונו ונוגעין בו בגלוי. הילכך, נגע שרץ בלשונו — טמאהו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:12:3.english: Capable of touching - It is exposed like his hands, for he extends his tongue and it is touched openly. Therefore, if a creeping animal touched his tongue, it renders him impure.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:13:1.english: Is considered concealed - And there is no need for the entry of water into the inside of the mouth.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:13:2.hebrew: אף כל מאבראי - ולא שיכניס מים לתוך הפה. ואף להוציא כל הלשון אינו יכול, וטבילה למקצת לא אשכחינן; אבל נגיעה — בכל שהוא הויא נגיעה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:13:2.english: So too everything [that requires immersion is] on the outside - And not that he must bring water into the mouth. And even to stick out the entire tongue he is unable, and we do not find immersion of a part [of a limb]; but [with regard to] contact [with impurity], contact with any amount is [considered] contact.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:14:1.hebrew: רבי - דריש: ״על הטמא וחטאו״ — חטוי על מקום טומאה הוי חטוי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:14:1.english: Rabbi - [He] expounds: “Upon the impure person... and he shall purify him” — sprinkling upon a place of impurity is [valid] sprinkling.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:15:1.hebrew: רבי - דריש ״על הטמא וחטאו״ — חטוי על מקום טומאה הוי חטוי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:15:1.english: Rabbi - Expounds “upon the impure [person]... and he shall purify him”: Purification upon a place of impurity is [valid] purification.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:16:1.hebrew: ורבנן סברי וחטאו וכבס בגדיו ורחץ - בעינן חטוי שיפול על מקום הראוי לרחיצה, דהיינו טבילה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:16:1.english: And the Rabbis maintain: “And he shall purify him... and he shall wash his clothes and bathe” - We require that the sprinkling fall upon a place that is fit for bathing, that is, immersion.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:17:1.english: Purification from purification - Sprinkling from immersion.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:18:1.hebrew: והצריכה רבי טבילה אחרת - משום חציצה, אלמא בעי ביאת מים לתוך הפה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:18:1.english: And Rabbi required her [to perform] another immersion - Because of an interposition; evidently, the entry of water into the mouth is required.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:1:2.english: That it is counted on the back of the hand - That it was in the row of the other fingers.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:20:1.hebrew: כר' זירא דאמר - במנחות (דף קג:): אין מביאין מנחה של ששים ואחד עשרון בכלי אחד, דקים להו לרבנן שאין נבללין יפה בשוין ביחד. והוינן בה: וכי אין נבללין, מאי הוי? והא אנן תנן: אם לא בלל — כשר! ואמר רבי זירא עלה: כל הראוי לבילה — אין בילה מעכבת בו, ואפי' לא בלל — כשר; וכל שאין ראוי לבילה, כגון ששים ואחד — בילה מעכבת בו, דראוי לבילה בעינן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:20:1.english: In accordance with Rabbi Zeira, who said - In Menachot (daf 103b): One may not bring a meal-offering of sixty-one issaron measures in a single vessel, for the Sages have established that they do not mingle well and evenly together. And we discussed it: Even if they do not mingle, what of it? Behold, we learned [in a Mishnah]: If one did not mingle [it], it is valid! And Rabbi Zeira said regarding this: Anything that is suitable for mingling, mingling is not indispensable for it, and even if one did not mingle [it], it is valid; but anything that is not suitable for mingling, such as sixty-one [measures], mingling is indispensable for it, for we require that it be suitable for mingling.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:2:1.english: The Elders of Nezonya - [Nezonya is] the name of a place.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:2:2.hebrew: זיל צנעינהו - אמור אליהם להסגר ולישב בבית. וזה לשון נדוי לתלמיד חכם, כדאמר במועד קטן (דף יז.), לאמר לו דרך כבוד: הסגר ושב בביתך:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:2:2.english: Go and ostracize them - Tell them to sequester themselves and sit at home. And this is the expression of ostracism for a Torah scholar, as [the Gemara] says in Moed Katan (17a), to say to him in a respectful manner: “Sequester yourself and sit in your house.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:3:1.hebrew: כמומין שבגלוי דמי - שהרי תלויין בכיס וניכרים מבחוץ, או לא, הואיל וטמונין בתוך הכיס:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:3:1.english: Is it considered like exposed blemishes - For they hang in the scrotum and are noticeable from the outside; or [is it] not, since they are hidden within the scrotum?

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:3:2.hebrew: קרנונא - יושב קרנות אתה, ולא בעל תורה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:3:2.english: Karnuna - You are a sitter at [street] corners, and not a master of Torah.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:4:1.hebrew: מתניתא בעו מינך - גרסינן, דמברייתא דתני עלה דמתניתין: "רבי אומר אף הסירוס" — יליף לה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:4:1.english: They asked of you a baraita - This is the reading, for from the baraita that is taught concerning the mishna, "Rabbi says: Even castration," he derives it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:4:2.hebrew: אין מטמאין משום מחיה - שם אחד מן הנגעים, כדכתיב (ויקרא י״ג:י׳): ״ומחית בשר חי בשאת״, וכתיב בה (שם): ״לכל מראה עיני הכהן״ — שתהא כולה נראית כאחת, פרט למחיה שהיא במקום המשופע ויורד לכל צד, שאין יכול לראות ראש הנגע ורגליו כאחת:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:4:2.english: Do not become impure on account of raw flesh - [This is] the name of one of the [types of] leprous afflictions, as it is written: “And quick raw flesh in the swelling” (Leviticus 13:10), and it is written regarding it: “To the entire sight of the priest’s eyes” (ibid.) — [meaning] that all of it must be visible at once, excluding [a patch of] raw flesh that is in a place that is sloped and descends on all sides, where one cannot see the top of the affliction and its bottom at once.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:5:1.english: And the extremities of the ears - The rim of the ear.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:5:2.english: The extremity of the body - The penis.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:5:3.hebrew: וראשי דדים שבאשה - אבל שבאיש אינן בולטין כל כך, ואין זה שיפוע:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:5:3.english: And the tips of the breasts of a woman - But those of a man do not protrude so much, and this is not [considered] a slope.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:5:4.hebrew: לחירות - דכולן, אם קצצו לו רבו, מום שבגלוי הוא ואינו חוזר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:5:4.english: To freedom - For [with regard to] all of them, if his master severed [it] for him, it is an exposed blemish and does not regenerate.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:5:5.hebrew: רבי אומר היזה - דאע"ג דהזאה על הגלוי בעינן, כדלקמיה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:5:5.english: Rabbi says: He has sprinkled - For even though we require sprinkling [to be] on an exposed [part of the body], as [stated] below.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:5:6.hebrew: רבי אומר אף הסירוס - מוסיף על אלו לענין עבד. ושן ועין לא איצטריך ליה לרבי למנות בתוספתא, דבהדיא כתיב, וזיל קרי בי רב הוא; ות"ק לא פליג בהא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:5:6.english: Rabbi says: Also castration - [He] adds [this] to these [limbs] regarding a slave. And tooth and eye, Rabbi did not need to enumerate in the Tosefta, as it is explicitly written [in the Torah], and it is [a matter of] 'go read in the schoolhouse' [i.e., elementary Scripture]; and the first tanna does not disagree about this.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:5:7.hebrew: אף הלשון - שדרכו ליראות כשהוא מדבר, ומום שבגלוי הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:5:7.english: Also the tongue - For it is normally seen when he speaks, and it is an exposed blemish.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:6:1.english: The Master said, etc. - Rav Ḥisda continues his statement to resolve the dilemma of the Elders.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:6:2.hebrew: היינו גוייה - דאימני לענין נגעים, ובכולהו אמר ת"ק: עבד יוצא לחירות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:6:2.english: This is geviyyah - For it was enumerated regarding leprosy, and regarding all of them the First Tanna said: A slave goes out to freedom.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:6:3.hebrew: ואלא דביצים - ש"מ, בעיא דסבי פלוגתא דרבנן ורבי היא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:6:3.english: And rather, of the testicles - Learn from this [that] the dilemma of the Elders is a dispute between the Rabbis and Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi].

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:7:1.hebrew: ה"ג ולרבי לשון לא - ולרבי, לשון לא הוי מום גלוי? — בתמיה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:7:1.english: This is the reading: And according to Rabbi, [is] the tongue not? - And according to Rabbi, is the tongue not an exposed blemish? — [asked] in astonishment.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:7:2.english: On his mouth - Of the impure person.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:7:3.hebrew: רבי אומר היזה - דאע"ג דהזאה על הגלוי בעינן, כדלקמיה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:7:3.english: Rabbi says: He has sprinkled - For even though we require sprinkling [to be] on an exposed [part of the body], as [stated] below:

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:8:1.hebrew: דחלים - סוגר פיו בחזקה עד ששפתיו נדבקות מאד, ולא נשוינהו כגלוי, הואיל ופעמים הם טמונות ע"י חלומו — קמ"ל. חלים — דבר שהוא מדביק יפה, שולדו"ר (שולדי"ר: ללחוץ בחזקה) בלע"ז, כדאמרינן גבי תפירות עור בהעור והרוטב (חולין דף קכג:): שאני עור דחלים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:8:1.english: That he closes [his lips] tightly - He closes his mouth tightly until his lips adhere very closely [together], and [lest one say that] we should not treat them as exposed, since at times they are hidden by means of his closing [them] tightly — [the baraita] teaches us [that they are considered exposed]. [The word] chalim [means] something that adheres well, soulder (to press firmly) in Old French, as we say regarding stitches of hide in [the chapter entitled] Ha’or VeHaRotev (Chullin 123b): “A hide is different, as it adheres [tightly].”

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:9:1.english: That most of the tongue was removed - With regard to the blemishes of a firstborn, they taught [this] in [tractate] Bekhorot.

Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:9:2.hebrew: רוב המדבר - ממקום פרישת דיבוקו ולמעלה קרי מדבר. אע"ג דדיבור בבהמה לא שייכא, קרי ליה מדבר, הואיל והוא המדבר בלשון האדם:
Rashi on Kiddushin 25a:9:2.english: Most of the speaking [part] - From the point where its attachment separates and upward is called "the speaking [part]." Even though speech does not apply to an animal, he calls it "the speaking [part]" since that is [the part] that speaks in a person's tongue.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 25a:14:1.hebrew: רבי מדמה ליה לטומאה - וא"ת: מאי פריך לעיל מהזה על לשונו? דילמא הזאה שאני, דאיתקש לטומאה, אבל לענין ראשי אברים מדמינן לטבילה? וי"ל: דע"כ ליכא לדמויי לטבילה, שהרי שן ועין — דהוו גלויי לעבד, שהוא יוצא בהן לחירות, ולגבי טבילה הוו כטמון, כדמסיק בסמוך דלא בעינן ביאת מים:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 25a:14:1.english: "Rabbi compares it to impurity" - And if you say: Why did [the Gemara] challenge above from [one who] sprinkled upon his tongue? Perhaps sprinkling is different, as it is juxtaposed to impurity, but with regard to the extremities of limbs [for emancipating a slave], we should compare [them] to immersion? And one can say: Perforce, one cannot compare [them] to immersion, for a tooth and an eye are [considered] exposed with regard to a slave, as he goes free on their account, yet regarding immersion they are considered concealed, as [the Gemara] concludes nearby that we do not require the entry of water.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 25a:20:1.hebrew: כל הראוי לבילה כו' - עיקר מילתא דר' זירא בפ' המנחות והנסכים (מנחות דף קג.), דתנן: אם אמר "הרי עלי מנחה של ששים ואחד עשרון" — מביא ששים בכלי אחד, והאחד בפני עצמו. ומפרש בגמרא: משום דששים נבללין, וס"א אין נבללין. ופריך: כי אין נבללין מאי הוי? והתנן: אם לא בלל — כשר! אמר ר' זירא: כל הראוי לבילה — אין בילה מעכבת, ואפי' לא בלל — כשר; וכל שאין ראוי לבילה — בילה מעכבת בו, דראוי לבילה בעינן. ואם תאמר: מאי פריך "ואם לא בלל כשר"? נהי דבלילה לא מעכבא, היינו דוקא בדיעבד, אבל לכתחילה מצוה לבלול! ויש לומר: דכיון דהאי גברא למנחה גדולה קמכוין, אם איתא דבעלמא כשר בדיעבד — בהאי גברא שהתנדב קרבן גדול שרי אף לכתחילה. עוד יש לומר: דאיכא נפקותא אליבא דמ"ד התם: אפילו המתנדב מנחה גדולה אינו מביא אלא לוג אחד. אם כן, כשהתנדב ס"א עשרונים, יצטרך להביא בשני כלים, לפי שאין נבללים יפה, ויצטרך להביא שני לוגים שמן, והוא לא התנדב אלא לוג אחד, והוי כמו ייתור שמנו, דקיימא לן (מנחות יא.) דייתור שמנו פסול. ואי הוה שרי בדיעבד בכלי אחד, היה טוב להביא לכתחילה, שלא יבא לידי ייתור שמן. ומיהו קשה: מ"ט דראוי? אי שנה הכתוב בלילה לעכב — ליבעי בלילה ממש! ואי לא שנה — אפילו ראוי לא ליבעי! וי"ל: דודאי שנה הכתוב "בלול" כמה פעמים, אבל לא כתב בלשון צווי ובלילה; משמע דאתא לאשמועינן דלא בעינן אלא ראוי. וא"ת: בטבילה מנ"ל דבעינן ראוי? ויש לומר: משום דכתיב "ורחץ את כל בשרו", דמשמע אפי' בית הסתרים, וכתיב "וידיו", ודרשינן: מה ידיו מאבראי אף כל מאבראי, וממעטים בית הסתרים; מ"מ, כיון דאיכא "כל" דמרבינן אפי' בית הסתרים, איכא למימר: לכל הפחות להכי מרבי, דבעינן ראוי לביאת מים:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 25a:20:1.english: "Whatever is fit for mingling, etc." - The primary context of Rabbi Zeira's statement is in the chapter [entitled] HaMenachot VeHaNesakhim (Menachot 103a), as we learned in a Mishnah: If one said, "It is incumbent upon me [to bring] a meal-offering of sixty-one tenths [of an ephah]," he brings sixty in one vessel and the one by itself. And the Gemara explains: Because sixty can be mingled [in a single vessel], but sixty-one cannot be mingled. And [the Gemara] objects: Even if they cannot be mingled, what of it? Didn't we learn in a Mishnah: If he did not mingle [it], it is valid! Rabbi Zeira said: [For] anything that is fit for mingling, mingling is not indispensable [for it], and even if he did not mingle it, it is valid; but [for] anything that is not fit for mingling, mingling is indispensable for it, as we require [that it be] fit for mingling. And if you say: Why does [the Gemara] object, "And didn't we learn: If he did not mingle [it], it is valid"? Granted that mingling is not indispensable, that is specifically after the fact (bedi'avad), but ab initio (lekhatchilah) it is a mitzva to mingle! And one can say: Since this person intends [to bring] a single large meal-offering, if it is so that generally [failure to mingle] is valid after the fact, for this person who pledged a large offering, it should be permitted even ab initio. Furthermore, it can be said: There is a practical halakhic difference according to the one who said there [that] even one who pledges a large meal-offering brings only one log [of oil]. If so, when he pledged sixty-one tenths [of an ephah], he would have to bring [them] in two vessels because they are not mingled well, and he would have to bring two logs of oil, whereas he only pledged one log; and this would be like an excess of its oil, and we maintain (Menachot 11a) that an excess of its oil renders [a meal-offering] invalid. And if it were permitted after the fact in one vessel, it would have been preferable to bring [it in one vessel] ab initio, so that he would not come to [a situation of] excess oil. However, it is difficult: What is the rationale for [requiring that it be] fit [for mingling]? If Scripture repeated [the requirement of] mingling to make it indispensable, let it require actual mingling! And if it did not repeat [it], it should not require even [that it be] fit [for mingling]! And one can say: Scripture certainly repeated [the word] "mingled" [balul] several times, but it did not write it in the language of a command and mingling [as an action]; this implies that it comes to teach us that we require only that it be fit [for mingling]. And if you say: With regard to immersion, from where do we know that we require [concealed parts of the body to be] fit [for the entry of water]? And one can say: Because it is written: "And he shall wash all his flesh" [Leviticus 15:16], which implies even concealed parts [of the body], and it is written: "and his hands" [Leviticus 15:11], and we expound: Just as his hands are on the outside, so too all [parts of the body required to be washed must be] on the outside, which excludes concealed parts; nevertheless, since there is [the word] "all," from which we include even concealed parts, one can say that at the very least it includes [them] for this [purpose]: that we require [them to be] fit for the entry of water.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 25a:3:1.hebrew: המנונא קרנונא - פי' בקונטרס: "יושב קרנות אתה, ולא בעל תורה". ור"ח פירש: אתה אומר "המנונא" — היינו "חם נונא", דג חם; ואין כן, אלא "קר נונא" — דג שהוא קר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 25a:3:1.english: "Hamnuna... Karnuna" - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: "You are one who sits at street corners [an idler], and not a master of Torah." And Rabbeinu Chananel explained: You say [your name is] "Hamnuna" — that is, cham nuna, a hot fish; but it is not so, rather [it is] kar nuna — a fish that is cold.
